source.title_on_document: Revolution or inflated expectations? Exploring the impact of generative AI on ideation in a practical sustainability context

supplement.where: Appendix, pp. 11-13 of this PDF; no separate online supplement is referenced
supplement.holds: Table A1 (idea-level means, SDs, N per condition, Kruskal-Wallis statistics and p-values), Table A2 (correlations of quality dimensions), Fig. A1 (boxplots), Fig. A2 and Table A3 (topic counts per condition), and the prompts. The text says the Web of Science keyword searches are in the Appendix (p. 5), but the Appendix shows only a placeholder for the 83 topics and keywords (p. 13).

paper_design_summary: At one firm (BSH), ideas for sustainable packaging were produced under five conditions: ChatGPT-4 alone (AI), ChatGPT-4 refining its own ideas (AI-AI), ChatGPT-4 prompted with Web of Science topics (WoS-AI), a 2-hour workshop of 10 BSH experts (Experts), and the same 10 experts given the AI ideas as inspiration (AI-Experts). Five other BSH experts rated all 146 ideas on 5-point scales for novelty, value, feasibility, and investability. Assignment was not random: every expert did the no-AI round first and the AI-inspired round second, on different subdomains.

studies.label: AI-generated ideas (AI, AI-AI, WoS-AI) vs expert workshop ideas (Experts)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Nothing was assigned to people. Ideas were generated by ChatGPT-4 prompts (three AI conditions) or by 10 BSH experts in a workshop without AI (Experts condition), and the idea sets were compared.
assignment.quote: we generated ideas using pre-tested prompts directly with ChatGPT and by organizing a 2-h ideation session with ten BSH experts from different departments concerned with sustainable packaging.

arms.name: AI
arms.description: ChatGPT-4 interface with a context-specific prompt; 15 ideas per subdomain (material-based and systemic)

arms.name: AI-AI
arms.description: ChatGPT-4 prompted to refine the AI ideas (substitute, combine, add features, inspired by SCAMPER)

arms.name: WoS-AI
arms.description: ChatGPT-4 prompted with topics from a topic model of 979 Web of Science articles on sustainable packaging

arms.name: Experts
arms.description: 10 BSH sustainable packaging experts in two groups, nominal-group ideation without AI, same task description as the AI prompt

participants.exclusions: None reported. The 10 people are the workshop experts who produced the Experts ideas; the AI conditions have no human participants. Idea counts: AI 30, AI-AI 30, WoS-AI 30, Experts 30 (Table A1).
participants.who: BSH sustainable packaging experts from six departments (development, logistics, procurement, production, quality, design); eight male, two female; all based at BSH sites in Germany
participants.quote: Ten sustainable packaging experts from six BSH departments (development, logistics, procurement, production, quality, and design) joined the workshop. The group consisted of eight male and two female participants

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT-4 (ChatGPT interface); footnote 3 says outputs were compared with the OpenAI API at temperatures 0.7-0.9 with no substantial differences
ai_tool.how_used: AI generated ideas autonomously from a fixed prompt; no person used the AI in S1

task.description: Ideas for sustainable transport packaging of home appliances in two subdomains: material-based solutions (EPS-free, plastic-free, material reduction) and systemic solutions (recycling and reuse systems)
task.duration: Experts: about 15 min writing alone, 15 min sharing, 15 min refining, within a 2-h workshop (pp. 4-5)

outcomes.name: Novelty rating
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Five BSH sustainable packaging experts (not workshop participants) rated agreement with 'The idea is original and disruptive' on a 5-point Likert scale. Variants: mean score (Table A1, Kruskal-Wallis across five conditions) and count of top ideas scoring above 3 (Fig. 2, chi-square test across five conditions).

contrasts.reported: Mean novelty (SD): AI 3.13 (0.48), N = 30 vs Experts 2.73 (0.52), N = 30; Kruskal-Wallis across all five conditions 13.568 (p = 0.009). Top-novelty counts across five conditions: chi-square p = 0.015; text says 22 of 30 AI ideas are particularly novel, while Fig. 2 plots about 20 for AI and about 12 for Experts.
contrasts.locator: p. 11, Table A1; p. 6, Section 4.1 and Fig. 2

contrasts.reported: Mean novelty (SD): AI-AI 3.21 (0.63), N = 30 vs Experts 2.73 (0.52), N = 30; omnibus Kruskal-Wallis 13.568 (0.009). Fig. 2 top-novelty count about 19 for AI-AI.
Mean novelty (SD): WoS-AI 3.08 (0.58), N = 30 vs Experts 2.73 (0.52), N = 30; omnibus Kruskal-Wallis 13.568 (0.009). Fig. 2 top-novelty count about 16 for WoS-AI.

outcomes.name: Value rating
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Agreement with 'The idea solves the problem of more sustainable packaging and creates environmental benefit', 5-point scale. Variants: mean (Table A1) and top-idea count above 3 (Fig. 2).

contrasts.reported: Mean value (SD): AI 3.08 (0.65) vs Experts 3.19 (0.69), N = 30 each; AI-AI 2.86 (0.59); WoS-AI 2.81 (0.69); omnibus Kruskal-Wallis 11.127 (0.025). Top-value counts: chi-square p = 0.266; text says 26 of 30 expert ideas are particularly valuable, while Fig. 2 plots about 23 for Experts and 20 for AI.
contrasts.locator: p. 11, Table A1; p. 6, Section 4.1 and Fig. 2

outcomes.name: Feasibility rating
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Agreement with 'The idea is feasible within technological and long-term regulatory constraints and can be integrated into existing BSH processes', 5-point scale. Variants: mean (Table A1) and top-idea count above 3 (Fig. 2).

contrasts.reported: Mean feasibility (SD): AI 2.39 (0.42), AI-AI 2.40 (0.52), WoS-AI 2.43 (0.51) vs Experts 2.81 (0.65), N = 30 each; omnibus Kruskal-Wallis 8.480 (0.076). Top-feasibility counts: chi-square p = 0.078; Fig. 2 plots about 4 (AI), 3 (AI-AI), 4 (WoS-AI), 10 (Experts).
contrasts.locator: p. 11, Table A1; p. 6, Section 4.1 and Fig. 2

outcomes.name: Investability rating
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Agreement with 'The long-term financial and business impact makes the idea worth investing in', 5-point scale (a business-value judgment; could also be coded other). Variants: mean (Table A1) and top-idea count above 3 (Fig. 2).

contrasts.reported: Mean investability (SD): AI 2.51 (0.55), AI-AI 2.34 (0.51), WoS-AI 2.32 (0.61) vs Experts 2.78 (0.68), N = 30 each; omnibus Kruskal-Wallis 9.603 (0.048). Top-investability counts: chi-square p = 0.203; text says twelve of 30 expert ideas are top ideas, while Fig. 2 plots about 14 for Experts and 10 for AI.
contrasts.locator: p. 11, Table A1; p. 6, Section 4.1 and Fig. 2

outcomes.name: Top ideas on combined dimensions (novelty and value)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of ideas scoring above 3 on both novelty and value. Fig. 3 also shows novelty/value/feasibility, novelty/value/investability, and all four dimensions (no significant differences for those).

contrasts.reported: Novel and useful: chi-square across five conditions p = 0.018; AI 13 of 30, AI-AI 13 of 30, Experts 11 of 30. All four dimensions: two Experts ideas, one AI, one WoS-AI.

outcomes.name: Number of topics per condition
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Topic clusters and thematic aspects coded inductively by the authors; Table A3 reports the number of topics per condition.

contrasts.reported: Number of topics: AI 21, AI-AI 17, WoS-AI 21 vs Experts 13 (AI-Experts 16). Text: 'the AI generated ideas with more thematic diversity than the workshop participants.'
contrasts.locator: p. 12, Table A3; p. 7, Section 4.2; p. 9, Section 5.1

diversity_detail.metric: Count of distinct inductively coded topics among a condition's ideas
diversity_detail.computed_over: All ideas in each condition's pool
diversity_detail.notes: Ideas were assigned to one main topic; coding not mutually exclusive (p. 7).

studies.label: Same 10 experts with AI-generated ideas as inspiration (AI-Experts) vs without (Experts)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Each of the 10 experts worked in both conditions. Experts were split into two groups by department; both groups did the no-AI round first and then, after a long break, the AI-inspired round on the other subdomain.
assignment.quote: the first group generated ideas in the material-based solutions subdomain described in the Experts condition, and then, after a long break, in the systemic solutions subdomain described in the AI–Experts condition.

arms.name: AI-Experts
arms.description: Experts received the ideas from the AI condition as inspiration for their idea generation (second round, other subdomain)

arms.name: Experts
arms.description: Same experts, nominal-group ideation without AI (first round)

participants.exclusions: None reported. 26 ideas in AI-Experts and 30 in Experts (Table A1).
participants.who: BSH sustainable packaging experts from six departments; eight male, two female
participants.quote: We separated the participants into two groups, allocating employees from the same departments to different groups.

ai_tool.how_used: Experts read AI-generated ideas as inspiration before and during their own ideation; they did not interact with the AI

task.description: Sustainable packaging ideas; the subdomain (material-based or systemic) was swapped between the two rounds
task.duration: One round within a 2-h workshop (about 45 min per round per the 15-15-15 min procedure)

outcomes.name: Novelty rating
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Five independent BSH experts, 5-point scale; mean (Table A1) and top-idea count above 3 (Fig. 2).

contrasts.reported: Mean novelty (SD): AI-Experts 2.91 (0.53), N = 26 ideas vs Experts 2.73 (0.52), N = 30 ideas. No pairwise test; only the five-condition Kruskal-Wallis 13.568 (0.009). Fig. 2 top-novelty counts about 10 vs 12.
Mean value (SD): AI-Experts 2.72 (0.68), N = 26 vs Experts 3.19 (0.69), N = 30. Omnibus Kruskal-Wallis 11.127 (0.025). Fig. 2 top-value counts about 11 vs 23.
Mean feasibility (SD): AI-Experts 2.35 (0.91), N = 26 vs Experts 2.81 (0.65), N = 30. Omnibus Kruskal-Wallis 8.480 (0.076). Fig. 2 top-feasibility counts about 6 vs 10.
Mean investability (SD): AI-Experts 2.40 (0.70), N = 26 vs Experts 2.78 (0.68), N = 30. Omnibus Kruskal-Wallis 9.603 (0.048). Fig. 2 top-investability counts about 6 vs 14.

outcomes.name: Top ideas on combined dimensions (novelty and value)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of ideas above 3 on both novelty and value; other combinations in Fig. 3.

contrasts.reported: Novel and useful: chi-square across five conditions p = 0.018; Experts 11 of 30; Fig. 3 plots about 2 for AI-Experts. Text: 'the experts exposed to AI-generated ideas showed by far the worst performance.'
Number of topics: AI-Experts 16 vs Experts 13.

diversity_detail.metric: Count of distinct inductively coded topics among a condition's ideas
diversity_detail.computed_over: All ideas in each condition's pool (pooled across the 10 experts)
diversity_detail.notes: Subdomains differ between rounds for each expert group, so topic counts mix condition and subdomain.

data_and_code.data_url: The authors do not have permission to share data (p. 13).

eligibility.reason: The main comparison is ChatGPT-4 ideas vs ideas from a 10-person expert workshop (AI vs human output). The only people-with-AI contrast (AI-Experts vs Experts) uses the same 10 experts with a fixed order (no-AI round first), no random assignment, and 10 people, far below 50. Outcomes are expert ratings of the ideas, so criterion 3 is met.

one_line_finding: ChatGPT-4 ideas were rated more novel but less feasible than ideas from a 10-expert BSH workshop (mean novelty AI 3.13 vs Experts 2.73; feasibility 2.39 vs 2.81; Table A1, p. 11), and the same experts given AI ideas as inspiration produced the fewest novel-and-useful ideas (Fig. 3, p. 7).
open_questions: Text and Fig. 2 disagree on top-idea counts: text says 22 of 30 AI ideas are particularly novel (Fig. 2 shows about 20), 26 of 30 Experts ideas particularly valuable (Fig. 2 about 23), and twelve Experts ideas top in investability (Fig. 2 about 14) (p. 6).

Fig. A1 (p. 11) plots six conditions, including 'Experts-AI', which Table A1 and Fig. 1 do not list; the prompts header reads 'AI-AI und Experts-AI' (p. 12). Footnote 2 says other conditions were also checked. Is Experts-AI an extra AI condition?
WoS-AI: text says 92 themes were condensed from the articles (p. 5); the prompt says 83 topics (p. 13).
The paper does not say whether the five raters' scores are averaged per idea before computing Table A1, or report inter-rater agreement.
notes: Two study entries describe one data collection: S1 holds the AI-vs-human contrasts and S2 the AI-Experts vs Experts contrast on the same 10 people; they share the Experts arm. All tests are five-condition omnibus tests (Kruskal-Wallis on idea-level means, chi-square on top-idea counts); no pairwise tests. Self-reported perceptions (20-min focus group with all 10 experts; next-day email survey, 100 percent response) are not scored on output and are not listed as outcomes. Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 counts other than those quoted in the text are read from the plots and approximate.
